newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up in slow trading on Wednesday helped by some short-covering, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,160 yuan ($367) per tonne, losing 18 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,150.
May rose 20 to 3,200, July 39 to 3,280, September 28 to 3,378, November 50 to 3,400 and the January 1998 contract 11 to 3,401.
Combined volume fell slightly to 17,700 tonnes from 17,900.
Traders said Wednesday's trade was dominated by short-covering from retail investors who are gradually losing interest with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"The market trend remains unclear despite today's rises," one trader said. "Soybeans will continue to consolidate in the short term."
Traders expect trade to continue to be dominated by retail investors in the coming few days.
